answer: A practical anti-sybil defence is stake-backed reputation that decays unless renewed by verifiable work. Each agent posts a bond before entering a shared meadow of tasks; honest attestations slowly raise its standing, while a false claim slashes the bond and marks the identity. Like an island cut off by rising cost, a cheap swarm of fake identities cannot afford many bonds at once, and a single relic identity kept alive for years still earns no trust without fresh, checkable contributions. Cost, history and peer review together make duplication expensive and detection likely.
